escena: SCENE (cinematic, high-impact editorial still, freeze-frame at 1/8000 s, a dark digital creative studio at night): a Chilean creative director in her early thirties, short dark curly hair with a few loose curls over her forehead, warm olive skin, small silver hoops, wearing the EFEONCE HOODIE, stands on the right side of the frame, framed from the waist up, REALISTIC ADULT PROPORTIONS, camera about two meters away at chest height, 85mm f/2. Her face is at about 62% of the frame width and at about one third of the frame height; her right elbow — the elbow nearest the frame-LEFT edge — is at about 47% of the frame width, and between the frame-left edge and her body there is a wide band of empty darkness. She holds BOTH hands forward at waist height, palms up and open, elbows relaxed, as she has just released ONE master key visual, and at this exact instant it EXPLODES just above her open palms into a fan of about a dozen finished pieces of content: THREE large ones just above her palms, sharp; FOUR mid-size ones halfway to the squad, soft; FIVE small ones near the squad, very blurred — each one the same campaign idea re-cut for its own format (slim 9:16 phone screen, 4:5 and square feed posts, a wide 16:9 video frame, a long web banner, a tall printed street poster; a different crop and layout of one bold key visual built from orange #FF6500, deep navy and white), so they read as one family, never as copies, all FROZEN perfectly still in the air. The fan leaves her palms toward the frame-right and the back of the room BELOW the height of her chest, so the embroidered mark on the hoodie chest stays fully visible, covered by no flying piece and grazed by the orange light only from below. At the root of the burst, just above her palms, burns a hot core of orange light (#FF6500), the only key light on her. A hard cool rim light from behind separates her hair and shoulders from the dark; no coloured panel on any wall; the BLUE of the frame is carried only by her Efeonce hoodie. Outside the orange core, the whole frame stays cool and contemporary: deep navy and near-black, nothing amber, golden or tungsten. She looks straight into the lens with a calm, knowing, closed-mouth smile, head almost frontal, both eyes and both eyebrows visible. Far behind her frame-right shoulder, small and out of focus in the haze, her squad works at three lit stations; nobody looks at the camera. Everything that tells the story — her face, her open palms, the three nearest pieces and the squad — sits between about 35% and 78% of the frame width; the burst and every flying piece never pass to the frame-left of her right elbow (the elbow nearest the frame-left edge), and her face stays clear of every flying piece. The frame-left part of the picture is calm, deep dark studio space: no lights at all, only the faint texture of the dark studio, no pieces, no people, no objects; the lower-left quarter stays the darkest, quietest area. Rich contrast, punchy color, no readable text on any piece, no logos of any other brand.
